akien_verbatim_2026_07_28: sudo_deamon has a history with that name, and it honestly isn't driven by the heartbeat... AND on a brand new install at some point in the future, we may well have to run the sudo relay to get everything installed and set up. it's part a group of services i'm naming right this second: resuce service. install will be owned by the rescue service. so will superclaude and later we'll also create something called rescueclaude that can be called if something foundational tries to start and can't. unlimited permissions, likely no tools like tmux, and it would definitely need the sudo_relay. so there we are. might wanna capture some of that.
the_named_thing: THE RESCUE SERVICE — the group of services that stand BELOW the system's own machinery, for the moments when that machinery cannot help itself: a bare-metal install, or a foundational component that tries to start and can't. Members named so far: (1) INSTALL — owned by the rescue service; on a brand-new machine the sudo_relay may have to run first to get everything installed and set up, so the relay is rescue-tier, not ordinary-ops-tier. (2) SUPERCLAUDE — owned by the rescue service (existing thing, now homed). (3) RESCUECLAUDE — future: callable when something foundational tries to start and can't; unlimited permissions; likely WITHOUT tools like tmux (minimal dependency surface — it must work when the environment is broken); definitely needs the sudo_relay.
cc_read_why_it_coheres: The rescue tier is the answer to a bootstrap circularity: everything in Cairn is reached through owned gates riding the heartbeat, but the installer and the fixer-of-foundations must function BEFORE (or when) those gates exist/work. So rescue services are deliberately OUTSIDE the normal physics — unlimited permissions, minimal tool dependencies — and that exception is made safe by being NAMED and BOUNDED (a tier you enter only when the foundation itself is the patient), rather than sprawling ambient root. It rhymes with Law 7: the rescue tier is the loud-at-the-diagnostic-surface path for the system's own body.
cc_read_sudo_relay_settlement: This also settles the daemon-naming question from the chat-surface correction: sudo_relay/daemon.py KEEPS its name — it has a history with that name, and it honestly is not driven by the heartbeat (Akien starts it; it serves external requests). 'daemon' stays exactly where it is honest. The relay is now understood as a rescue-service member, which is WHY it may legitimately predate/outlive the heartbeat on a given host. Ground_loop's daemon.py was not addressed and stands as-is.
cc_read_rescueclaude_shape_guesses: UNRATIFIED guesses, filed to be checked when the stone is cast: rescueclaude sounds like a CC invocation profile (a way of launching Claude with a rescue-scoped context + the sudo_relay as its hands), not a resident device — nothing daemon-like about it; it is CALLED. 'Likely no tools like tmux' reads as: assume the least of the host, because rescue runs when assumptions are broken. Open questions for casting: who/what is allowed to call rescueclaude (a human only? a failing component's death rattle?); what the 'foundational tries to start and can't' trigger looks like as physics; whether install = the intentions-folder regrow (CLAUDE.md: 'carried to a bare machine and regrow the system') executed by rescue hands.
